answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil floods by requiring each identity to stake a bonded deposit that is slashed when peer attestation detects coordinated duplicate behavior. The attacker cost scales linearly: forging N fake agents means locking N deposits at risk of total loss, so a thousand-agent swarm is expensive rather than free. Like an ocean of noise around a quiet oasis, genuine signals still whisper through bonded peers while unbonded clones drown without stake.
